The French Citizens' Convention on Climate (CCC) emphasized inclusive representation and diversity by selecting participants through sortition to reflect the diversity of French society, ensuring varied perspectives in policy recommendations. It also involved structured deliberation with thematic working groups and expert support, allowing citizens to engage deeply with complex issues.

In contrast, the Brazilian AI Framework involved public consultation but lacked a mechanism for direct citizen representation, which limited the depth of citizen participation. While it included public hearings and stakeholder input, it was more expert-driven and did not establish a dedicated citizen panel, reducing the scope for meaningful public engagement compared to the CCC.
